The lava lamp

Two liquids that will not mix, one light bulb, and a density that changes with heat: a slow convection engine, and a clock built around it.

01How it moves

The bulb warms the wax pooled on the coil. Wax expands more than the liquid, so above some temperature it is the lighter of the two and rises verified [1]. Near the cool top it gives up heat, grows denser and sinks; the coil breaks the surface tension of returning blobs so they merge again verified [1]. Fluid dynamicists file it as a form of Rayleigh–Taylor instability verified [1].

CCl₄≈ 60 % denser than water; once added to weigh the wax down; out of US lamps since 1970 verified [1]

The curves are schematic: the crossing is the point, not the numbers.

03Time in the base

The 1963 Astro’s gold base was pierced with small holes that glowed like starlight other source [5].

Ours spell the local time, 24-hour, on a 29 × 9 grid: the digits bright, every other hole a faint glow.

The wax is not the clock and never knows the time. Only the holes change, once a minute.

\ the liquid: a hot layer over the coil
: env  ( y -- T )  dup 0.08 / negate exp  0.75 *  0.3 +  swap 0.08 * - ;

A sketch. Phase 3 writes the real words and checks them step for step against the Python model. exp and expm1 are new engine words.

A3 portrait · 297 × 420 mm.

A3 poster, drawn at print size and scaled to fit

A layout draft on real, sourced text. The finished poster uses the repository's poster pipeline (Phase P): first a research document (docs/reference/lava-lamp-research.md), then make_poster.py and export_poster.py. These produce one 297 × 420 mm PDF page, a 300 DPI PNG and layout-review.json, guarded by a pytest.

Every printed claim carries a chip: verified (checked against the cited source), other source (a secondary or retail source, which the research document must confirm or cut) or ours (our model or design). make_poster.py refuses to build if any claim is unconfirmed.

The hero image on the sheet is this mockup's canvas lamp. The print uses a Cycles render of the shipped Blender scene, as the aquarium posters do.

The patent table links each number to Google Patents. The PDF keeps the links, and the print adds a QR code per row (Q8).

Panel 05 runs from Dunnet's 1950 filing to Cloudflare's wall of about 100 lamps in 2017. Events are spaced evenly, not to scale.

Q7, yes: the timeline includes 1959, when Craven Walker (as Michael Keatering) directed Travelling Light, the first naturist film released publicly in the UK.

Panel 06 is the movement code. Panel 07 lists the four ways to move the wax that the plan weighs (D6); the Forth model is ticked as recommended.
